name: Philosophy

rules_of_thumb: PL.M.H. Appeal to intuition. Appeal to a canon. "Category mistake" as a diagnosis that still needs an argument. A definition that settles a dispute by vocabulary is a stipulation and must say so. The named-fallacies list. Burden of proof as a dialectical convention.
collisions: A claim is placed by the sentence it makes, not by the department or century it comes from.
Logic as a claim about consequence is PL.O.A3.2. Calculi and metatheorems are MA.O.A1, cited as "uses MA.O.A1".
History of philosophy is reconstruction (PL.M.B5) of answers already placed on Face O. That a philosopher held a view at a date is HI.O.A1; whether the argument succeeds is PL.
Philosophy of X: entitlement to assert is A5; what X may enforce or ought to do is A4; what the X-object is, A1 or A2.
Philosophy of religion is PL. An argument from premises any reasoner may grant is PL.O.A1.1. Religious epistemology is PL.O.A2.2. The same conclusion argued from a creed is RE.O·T.
A moral claim argued from shared premises is PL.O.A4. One citing scripture, creed or school is RE·T. One reporting what a tradition holds is RE·S.
Normative legitimacy, obligation and justice are PL.O.A4.3. PO cites them; PO owns who holds power and how (PO).
The concept of law is PL.O.A4.3. Whether a norm is valid in a given legal system is LA (W10).
Causation in general is PL.O.A1.3. A legal causation test is LA; causal identification from data is EC (EC.B2 design), cited.
The hard problem and intentionality are PL.O.A2.3. Processing, measured, is MS.
Probability as measure is MA.O.A5; as an agent's choice model, EC.O.A1; its interpretation, PL.O.A5.3.
Curry–Howard is CS.O.A1.5; PL.O.A3.2 uses it, with the intuitionistic hypothesis stated.
A theorem, calculus or metatheorem of logic → MA.O.A1
A probability measure or limit theorem → MA.O.A5
Curry–Howard and type-theoretic programs → CS.O.A1.5
Measured cognition, perception or processing → MS
Who holds power, how institutions work → PO
Validity and duty under a named legal system → LA
A law of nature or physical formalism → PH
Population genetics, species data → BI

whether computational philosophy (M5) is a sixth role; the count would then break the 2–5 rule and need a merge.

question: : which metaphysical questions are distinct and jointly exhaustive?

holds Māori whakapapa read as an ontology of relational descent (Stewart, *Māori Philosophy*, 2021, per audit). The claim, not the community, sits here.

Modality. Possible worlds as a device; de re and de dicto; essentialism. Rule: a necessity claim must say which type it is: logical, metaphysical or nomological. Modal systems K, T, S4 and S5 as calculi are MA.O.A1; which one models metaphy
Causation, persistence and identity. Causation answers: regularity, counterfactual dependence, process, interventionist (Woodward 2003). Persistence answers: endurance, perdurance (Lewis 1986).

identity. Leibniz's law (the indiscernibility of identicals) holds for numerical identity in extensional contexts. It fails as a test inside belief and other opaque contexts. Trouble case: the statue and the clay.
personal identity is the identity question asked of persons. The psychology of the self is MS.

free will. Whether responsibility is compatible with determinism. Frankfurt cases (1969) (UNVERIFIED) target the principle of alternate possibilities. The empirical psychology of choice stays in MS (audit error 5).
holds al-Ghazālī's occasionalist critique of necessary causal connection (audit item; date UNVERIFIED).

name: Knowledge and mind
question: : which questions does this claim-type contain?
look_for: Knowledge. The analysis is a deductive group: truth, belief, and a further condition. Truth: a known falsehood is not knowledge.
belief condition. CONTESTED: Radford's unconfident examinee (1966) denies that knowledge entails belief. Williamson's knowledge-first view (2000) denies that knowledge is analysable at all.
further condition. Justified true belief is the standard post-Gettier framing; whether it was ever the received view is disputed (Dutant 2015).

Gettier cases (1963) assume two things. A false belief can be justified. Justification is closed under deduction the subject performs. Given both, justified true belief is not sufficient for knowledge.

replies to Gettier: one inductive group of five. No false lemmas (Clark 1963); causal connection (Goldman 1967); reliability; tracking (Nozick 1981); virtue (Sosa). This list replaces v1's two lists (audit error 6).
scepticism is not a member of that group. It claims the further condition is never met for a stated domain.
structure of justification: foundationalism, coherentism, externalism, as answers to the regress.
Sources of entitlement. Perception, memory, testimony, reason, introspection. Rationalism and empiricism are answers about source. A priori is a way of being entitled, not a place.
social epistemology: testimony and peer disagreement. Disagreement alone does not prescribe a unique revision.

epistemology of religion (audit error 19): religious experience, reformed epistemology (Plantinga), Hume on testimony to miracles. Boundary: the argument that scriptural authority is rational to accept is PL.O.A2.2. A claim resting on that
Mind. Identity theory, functionalism, eliminativism, dualism, as answers. Intentionality.
the hard problem (Chalmers 1995): why physical processing is accompanied by experience. Stated as a problem, not as a proof of dualism. MS defers here.
Searle's Chinese room (1980) assumes that running a program is purely syntactic manipulation. It concludes that syntax does not suffice for semantics.

the extended mind (Clark and Chalmers 1998); machine consciousness; perception (veridical and not); action as doing for a reason. Action sits here when the question is the mental cause, and in A4 when it is the reason's worth.
Yogācāra read as a theory of mind and appearance (audit item; CONTESTED, alternative A1.4).

name: Meaning and inference
question: : which questions does this claim-type contain, and where is the line with MA and LN?
look_for: Meaning. Reference and sense (Frege's puzzle: "a = a" is trivial, "a = b" can be informative). Use as meaning. Speech acts. Literal and implicated content as concepts.
truth-conditional semantics (Davidson 1967): to know a sentence's meaning is to know under which conditions it is true. It assumes a recursive truth theory for the language.
names: descriptivism against direct reference. Kripke's modal argument (1980) assumes proper names are rigid designators across possible worlds.
compositionality (Frege's principle) as a concept. Its empirical testing in a named language is LN.O.A3.
Grice's cooperative principle as a concept of conversational rationality. Implicature patterns in a language are LN.O.A3.
Consequence. Deduction preserves truth if valid. Induction does not, and can still be reasonable. Abduction infers to an explanation. Validity is form; soundness adds true premises.
explosion: from a contradiction anything follows, in classical and intuitionistic logic. Relevance and paraconsistent logics reject it.
holds which logic is correct, logical pluralism, and the significance of the liar and sorites paradoxes.

uses MA.O.A1 for metatheorems. Gödel's first incompleteness theorem holds for a consistent, effectively axiomatised theory that interprets elementary arithmetic. What it shows about mind or truth is PL.
uses CS.O.A1.5 for Curry–Howard. It pairs intuitionistic natural deduction with the simply typed lambda calculus. Classical logic needs control operators (Griffin 1990).
holds Mohist logic and Mīmāṃsā's hermeneutics of injunction as reconstructed consequence and meaning claims (audit items; Mīmāṃsā CONTESTED, alternative A3.1).
decision under uncertainty, when it is a consequence relation on credences. When the utilities are values, it is A4.2.

name: Value
question: : which value questions are distinct?
look_for: Metaethics. Cognitivism, expressivism, realism. The Frege–Geach problem: expressivism must explain how "lying is wrong" keeps its meaning inside a conditional.

Moore's open-question argument (1903, §13). It assumes a correct analysis of "good" would make "is N good?" closed to a competent speaker. Moore offered it for non-naturalism. Main reply: synthetic property identity (Putnam; Boyd).

Normative ethics, worked descent kept from v1. Key line inductive · answer-families · dimension the bearer of value · order outcome, constraint, character: consequentialism, deontology, virtue ethics.
a hybrid theory is not a fourth family until it says which bearer decides a conflict.
Kant's categorical imperative is one deontic construction; rights theories are another. A constraint that forbids a small harm and permits a disaster needs a threshold or an admission.
virtue rightness criterion (Hursthouse 1999): an act is right if a virtuous agent would characteristically do it in the circumstances.
applied ethics (audit error 15): life, war, animals, environment, technology, professional ethics, AI moral status and alignment ethics. A case is not a new theory.
owns the normative claim in professional and AI ethics. The professional duty as a legal duty is LA; the constraint on a specification is CS or EN.
Political and legal philosophy. Legitimacy of coercion, political obligation, liberty, equality, authority, justice. Owner for PO.O.A1 and LA.O.A1, which cite it.
Rawls (1971): parties behind a veil of ignorance, mutually disinterested and choosing under uncertainty, would choose the two principles. The maximin step assumes they cannot assign probabilities.
Nozick (1974): entitlement theory, assuming self-ownership and a just initial acquisition. Berlin (1958): negative and positive liberty. Cohen on egalitarian justice (UNVERIFIED work date).

the concept of law: positivism (Hart), interpretivism (Dworkin), natural law (Finnis 1980). CONTESTED: "what makes a norm law" is an entitlement question and fits A5 under the restated rule. Kept at A4.3 to keep PO and LA citing one cell.
philosophy of gender, race and sexuality, when the claim is about a social category and a harm. When the claim is about what the category picks out, it is A1.1.
Dussel's philosophy of liberation and critical theory's emancipation claim, as reconstructed political claims.
African personhood debate: Menkiti against Gyekye on whether personhood is acquired in community (audit item; CONTESTED, alternative A1.3).
Aesthetics. What a work is and why it merits attention. Intention, form, reception as answers. Hume's standard of taste (1757). Owner for AR, which applies criteria to named works.
the ontology of a musical work (type and token) is A1.1, as the AR prototype already cites.

name: Standing of the sciences and mathematics
question: : which entitlement questions does this cell hold, without absorbing any science?
look_for: General philosophy of science. Explanation, confirmation, law, model, reduction. A model is not the system.
underdetermination: more than one theory can fit the same finite evidence. It is a limit, not a licence to ignore evidence.
holds logical empiricism and naturalism as answers about entitlement (see PL.B.C5).
Natural sciences. Philosophy of physics: time, probability in physics, the measurement problem. The formalism stays in PH.
philosophy of chemistry (audit error 10): reduction of chemistry to physics; the chemical bond as a kind. The bond itself is CH.
philosophy of biology: function, species, units of selection. Population genetics stays in BI.
Formal sciences. Philosophy of mathematics: platonism, nominalism, structuralism, as answers to what a theorem is about. The proof stays in MA.
philosophy of probability: frequency, propensity, subjective and logical interpretations. The measure is MA.O.A5; the agent model is EC.O.A1. CONTESTED: alternative home A3.2.
philosophy of computing and information: what computation is, and whether information is physical. Cites CS.
Mind and social sciences. Philosophy of cognitive science: representation and explanation in cognitive models. Cites MS.
philosophy of social science: whether reasons are causes, and whether a social kind is like a natural kind. The data stay in MS, EC or PO.
philosophy of history: whether historical explanation is causal or interpretive. Cites HI; HI's historiography bridge cites this cell.
